Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G3551; lawless, i.e. (negatively) not subject to (the Jewish) law; (by implication, a Gentile), or (positively) wicked:--without law, lawless, transgressor, unlawful, wicked.
BiblicalUsage: The lawless are those who live outside God's law, whether men who never had it or the man of sin who defies it. Paul lists the lawless among those the law was made for, and the man of sin is revealed as the lawless one.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for the lawless carries no doctrine of its own; its warning is the apostles', that the law was written for those who live as if it did not exist.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
